# Implementer Report — T126: Retire the entry-level resolution status

## ROUND

Implementation round 1. No previous review (`PREV_REVIEW`) and no refactoring
flag were supplied with this dispatch.

## STATUS

DONE.

## SUGGESTION_RESOLUTIONS

No `CROSS_ISSUE_SUGGESTIONS` were supplied with this dispatch, so there is
nothing to accept, reject, or defer.

## SELF_REVIEW

### Contract check (docs/adr/0045 / ../TASK.md)

| Contract item | Status | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ExpectedSetEntry` no longer exposes a directory-level resolution status or its reason strings | Done | `crates/skill-index/src/lib.rs:64-84` (entry struct, no `resolution` field); `ResolutionStatus` survives only as `SkillFile::resolution` (`:60`) |
| Failure is derived from the Skill files the entry owns | Done | `ExpectedSetEntry::is_failed()` at `crates/skill-index/src/lib.rs:89-93`; `generate_manifest` now gates on `skill.is_failed()` at `:404-406` |
| Failed entries still name the missing location/reason | Done | `failed_entry` at `crates/skill-index/src/lib.rs:373-396` keeps the same reason strings and anchors them on the root missing `SkillFile`; exact-message assertions in `missing_vendor_directory_yields_failed_entry` (`:626-639`), `missing_upstream_directory_yields_failed_entry` (`:658-671`), `malformed_skill_path_reports_a_missing_root_skill_file` (`:904-926`), `variant_without_skill_file_reports_a_missing_skill_file` (`:957-980`) |
| No consumer reads the retired status | Done | `crates/deploy/src/dev.rs:29` already used `is_failed()`; `crates/deploy/src/pack.rs:172-201`, `crates/validation-runner/src/lib.rs:136-144`, `tests/test_toolkit_setup.rs:61-73` already read `SkillFile::resolution`; workspace compiles |
| Dev policy, pack strictness, tarball/installed layout, lock format, entry-state verdicts unchanged | Done | `pack.rs:23` still rejects failed entries before `generate_manifest` (`pack.rs:49`); dev still warns/blocks via `is_failed()`; no format or layout code touched |
| Existing assertions not weakened | Done | Every touched assertion became stricter (exact message equality/prefix instead of `contains`); the one removed assertion set (`assert_eq!(entry.resolution, Resolved)`) asserted the retired field and is replaced by `assert!(!entry.is_failed())` plus existing file checks |
| `cargo test --workspace` green | Done | See "Tests actually run" below |

### TDD discipline

Red step was captured before implementation: the new interface test
`entry_failure_is_derived_from_its_skill_files` constructed an
`ExpectedSetEntry` without `resolution` and failed to compile with
`error[E0063]: missing field 'resolution' in initializer of 'ExpectedSetEntry'`
in its `ExpectedSetEntry` literal. The field was then removed and the
test now passes. No behavior test was deleted.

### Divergence / notes

- `generate_manifest` previously skipped only entries whose **directory** was
  missing; it now skips any entry with a missing owned file (`is_failed()`).
  This is the ADR-0045 definition and cannot change packed output: `pack.rs`
  calls `reject_failed_entries` (`:23`) before `generate_manifest` (`:49`), so
  every entry reaching the manifest is already file-complete.
- `CONTEXT.md` "Expected-set entry" was the only stale prose; it now says
  failure is derived from the entry's Skill files.
- No unique behavior was dropped: missing-directory entries still carry one
  root `SkillFile` with the same `"vendor skill directory not found: …"`,
  `"upstream skill directory not found: …"`, or `"malformed skillPath …"`
  reason.
- Clippy was not run: the parent agent instructed a stop on further checks
  before I reached it. The workspace compiled cleanly under `cargo test`.
- `rust-script --test tests/test_build.rs` was started but aborted by the
  parent's stop instruction; it did **not** complete, so it is not claimed as
  passing.

## CHANGED_FILES

| File | Change |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/skill-index/src/lib.rs` | Removed `ExpectedSetEntry::resolution` (was `:83`) and its three initializers (upstream literal, `resolved_entry`, `failed_entry`); updated `ResolutionStatus`/entry docs; `generate_manifest` now uses `is_failed()`; added `entry_failure_is_derived_from_its_skill_files`; updated/strengthened entry, failure-message, and manifest tests; removed `resolution` from the `entry()` test helper |
| `crates/validation-runner/src/lib.rs` | Removed `resolution: ResolutionStatus::Resolved` from the `test_entry` fixture (`:523-543`); production code was already file-based and unchanged |
| `CONTEXT.md` | "Expected-set entry" definition now says failure is derived from the Skill files it owns (was: directory-level resolution) |
| `IMPLEMENTER_REPORT.md` | This report |

Verified, unchanged (pre-existing and already compliant): `crates/deploy/src/dev.rs`,
`crates/deploy/src/pack.rs`, `crates/validation-runner/src/lib.rs` production
paths, `tests/test_toolkit_setup.rs`, `docs/adr/0045-expected-set-entry-resolves-its-skill-files.md`.
`../TASK.md` was read only and is untouched.

## SUMMARY

Retired the entry-level resolution status as ADR 0045 specifies. An
`ExpectedSetEntry` is now just identity, source, source directory, and the
Skill files it owns; `is_failed()` is the single failure predicate, and
`generate_manifest` uses it. Missing-directory and malformed-provenance paths
still produce a failed entry whose root `SkillFile` carries the exact reason
string, so dev, pack, and validation messages are unchanged. Tests were updated
to pin the new interface and exact wording; the full Cargo workspace is green
and `tests/test_toolkit_setup.rs` passes.

## Tests actually run

1. **Red (before change)**: `cargo test -p skill-index --lib entry_failure_is_derived_from_its_skill_files`
   → compile error `E0063: missing field 'resolution' in initializer of 'ExpectedSetEntry'`
   in the test's `ExpectedSetEntry` literal.
